blocks.content: Ladakh's demography is defined by its extremely low population density, its roughly even Buddhist-Muslim split between its two districts, and its overwhelmingly tribal population composition — each a frequently tested comparative fact.

cells: approx 2.74 lakh (274,289) — one of the smallest populations of any Indian state/UT
approx 3 persons per sq km — the LOWEST population density of any Indian state or UT by a wide margin
Leh district: Buddhist-majority; Kargil district: Shia Muslim-majority — the two districts have roughly comparable population size

A very high proportion of Ladakh's population is classified as Scheduled Tribe (including Bot/Boto, Balti, Beda, Bodh, Changpa, Garra, Mon, Purigpa communities among others), among the highest ST population shares of any Indian district-level unit

Historically skewed, though improving; monastic celibacy traditions among a portion of the Buddhist population have historically been cited as one contributing structural factor alongside broader regional patterns

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Ladakh's population density (~3 persons/sq km) is the LOWEST of any Indian state or UT — an extreme outlier even compared to other sparsely populated Himalayan regions, and one of the most reliably tested superlative facts about this UT.

items: Leh district has a Buddhist majority, with Ladakhi Buddhism belonging to the Tibetan Vajrayana/Mahayana tradition, closely linked historically and doctrinally to Tibetan Buddhism (Chapter 10).

Kargil district has a Shia Muslim majority, reflecting historical trade and cultural links with neighbouring Baltistan (now in Pakistan-administered territory) and Central Asia — Ladakh's Muslim population is predominantly Shia, distinguishing it from the largely Sunni-majority Muslim population of the Kashmir Valley covered in the companion J&K GS volume.

Smaller communities include Sunni Muslims (concentrated particularly around Leh town's trading community, with historical Kashmiri and Central Asian trade links), Christians (a small minority linked to historical missionary activity), and the Arghons (a distinct Ladakhi Muslim community of mixed Kashmiri-Ladakhi/Balti heritage, traditionally associated with trade).

Ladakh's Scheduled Tribe communities (Chapter 9's table above) include the Changpa (semi-nomadic pastoralists of the Changthang plateau, Chapter 2), the Brokpa/Dard community (concentrated in the Dah-Hanu area along the Indus, noted for a distinct Indo-Aryan linguistic and cultural heritage differing from the Tibetan-influenced majority), and several other historically distinct groups.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Brokpa/Dard community of the Dah-Hanu area is a frequently tested distinctive-minority fact — unlike most of Ladakh's Tibetan-Buddhist-influenced population, the Brokpa are ethnically and linguistically Indo-Aryan/Dardic, with a documented, distinct cultural heritage sometimes highlighted in anthropological and tourism contexts.

items: Ladakhi (Bhoti), a Tibetic language closely related to Classical Tibetan, is the majority language of Leh district and much of the wider region, traditionally written using the Tibetan script.
Purgi (Purik), a related but distinct Tibetic/Balti-linked language variety, is more widely spoken in the Kargil district.

Urdu has historically served as an administrative and educational link language across the erstwhile combined state (and continues to hold significant use in Kargil in particular, given its historical association with the wider Muslim-majority administrative tradition), alongside Hindi and English in official and educational use.
Balti, Brokskat (spoken by the Brokpa/Dard community), and other minority languages/dialects are also present in specific localities.
Population (2011): approx 2.74 lakh; density approx 3 persons/sq km — the LOWEST of any Indian state/UT.
Leh district: Buddhist-majority; Kargil district: Shia Muslim-majority (distinct from Kashmir Valley's Sunni-majority Muslim population).
Very high Scheduled Tribe population share, including Bodh, Changpa, Balti, Purigpa, Beda, Garra, Mon and other communities.
Brokpa/Dard community (Dah-Hanu area): ethnically/linguistically Indo-Aryan-Dardic, distinct from Ladakh's predominant Tibetan-influenced culture.
Ladakhi (Bhoti) = majority language of Leh; Purgi (Purik) = majority language of Kargil; both are Tibetic languages.
